reports.text: Fisho’s Weekly Fishing Report – 27th November, 2026. Carl managed to find triple-tail cod after the recent flooding. An elusive species you can actively target during the wet season. A Wet Weekend Ahead Pleasant conditions over the past week were most enjoyable. It warmed up but humidity was low and nights were mild and comfortable. Looking forward, the next few days will be a tad different as the latest band of wet weather reaches our coastline. Yesterday’s spike in the south-easterly wind eased overnight, so those on the water today are enjoying a gentle 10-15 knots from the same direction with a slight threat of showers. The wind will tend more north-easterly to 15 knots Saturday as the frequency of showers increases. Sunday could see the 15-knot wind ease to 10 knots from the north initially, tending north-westerly through the day. Sunday will be wet, with showers leading to likely storms later. Naturally, humidity will build as the wet weather approaches then encompasses our region. More showers for the start of the working week, but Monday looks great. A brief south-easterly change thereafter followed by gentle onshore breezes looks appealing through the week. As Wednesday’s super moon has passed, the associated massive tides are abating as the moon wanes. The next half-moon of the third quarter phase is scheduled for Tuesday, when the neap tides thereabouts will once again start to ‘make’ thereafter. reports.text: Leukaemia breakthrough brings hope of better treatment. Leukaemia doesn’t discriminate. It can affect anyone, regardless of age, gender, race or religion, which is why my mum, Jo Jones, and I both supported the Leukaemia Foundation’s fundraising efforts. Every year from 2011, Mum lopped her silver locks for the foundation’s World’s Greatest Shave. Every year, except last year, when she sadly passed away. So it’s a shame she isn’t here to read about the latest research into chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), which could bring improved treatment options and quality of life for people living with the disease. There are more than 7000 people living with CML in Australia. A type of blood cancer, it is caused by a genetic abnormality that fuels the growth of abnormal blood cells. Medical advances mean that many patients can now manage the potentially life-threatening condition through medication, but only 25 per cent ever reach treatment-free remission. reports.text: No report this week due to inclement weather. Offshore opportunities have been limited this week, but a good weather window today produced some quality fish around Double Island Point. Cod, amberjack and pearl perch all featured in catches, with anglers making the most of the improving conditions. North Reef continues to produce quality pearl perch and snapper for anglers making the most of the weather windows. Further offshore, the Barwon Banks are fishing well for goldband snapper, Moses perch, tuskfish and pearl perch, with good numbers of fish being reported across the wider grounds. reports.text: Fisho's Weekly Fishing Report – 16th October, 2026. Dane was absolutely stoked with this beautiful permit he caught on fly whilst fishing at Weipa recently. Onshore Breeze Bringing Showers The weather has changed dramatically in recent days; from the previously steamy heat spawned by northerly winds to much cooler and breezier conditions with an increasing threat of showers. As pleasant and comfortable as our climate feels right now, it is hard to visualise any joy for boaties beyond sheltered waters for a few days to come. Today's 15 knot easterly is set to strengthen slightly during Saturday and restrict boaties all weekend. Winds are likely to kick-off each day at 15 knots then build to 20 if not 25 knots. Saturday looks the worst, with a subtle improvement possible Sunday. The chance of showers is increasing day by day too. Not enough to soak our parched landscape, but welcome all the same if we can get a few mm per day. Gradually improving weather into the next working week will open up opportunities for frustrated boaties. The high-pressure system that has stalled in the Tasman Sea will hopefully weaken enough to see winds lighten. Offshore will still be limited to larger vessels, but the eastern and southern bay should be okay. The moon is waxing again after the passing of the new moon phase last Sunday. Monday will see in the half-moon of the latest first quarter phase, which means neap tides and minimal current flow once again. Happy days for those folks keen to tang

reports.text: Wet and windy conditions are expected this weekend, so anglers will be best served heading up the creeks to escape the worst of the showers and south-easterly winds. With the overcast conditions, mangrove jacks should be high on the target list. Surface lures such as frogs and 70-90mm poppers worked tight against snaggy structure are worth a look, while live baits and fresh strips of mullet continue to produce fish. Even when the jacks are quiet, there are usually plenty of cod and bream around to keep rods bending. A few stocked Tin Can Bay barramundi have also been caught over the past couple of weeks as water temperatures continue to rise. Live baits have accounted for some captures, while slowly worked soft plastic prawns remain a reliable option. Crabbing has been a little quiet, although the recent rainfall should help get the crabs moving. It’s still worth setting a few pots, with fresh baits and a longer soak generally producing the best results.
reports.credit: Coastwatch (Tin Can Bay section by The Chandlery Bait & Tackle)

reports.text: Mackerel remain the headline act across the region, with broadbar and school mackerel dominating catches around the Urangan Pier, local beaches and the wider bay. The pier is also producing quality queenfish, giant trevally, golden trevally and the occasional Spanish mackerel, while whiting continue to be caught along the Hervey Bay foreshores and throughout the Great Sandy Straits. The Great Sandy Straits and local river systems are fishing well for grunter, flathead, threadfin salmon, blue salmon and barramundi. Mangrove jacks are firing throughout the western creeks and the Burrum system, while quality whiting are also featuring in the middle reaches. Offshore, coral trout, grassy sweetlip, cod and Spanish mackerel continue to feature, while billfish activity is building with juvenile black marlin, striped marlin and yellowfin tuna all being reported. Around Rooneys Point and Station Hill, the first consistent run of juvenile black marlin for the season has provided plenty of excitement for gamefishers. Fraser Island’s tailor season remains patchy depending on location and conditions, although quality greenbacks are still being caught through the central sector. Anglers are also finding dart, whiting and the occasional trevally along the surf beaches. Boaties should remain aware of lingering whale traffic and patches of nuisance “snot weed” in parts of Platypus Bay and the central bay.
reports.credit: Coastwatch (Tin Can Bay section by The Chandlery Bait & Tackle)

reports.text: There are still some quality flathead being caught through the lower reaches of the Noosa River, with a number of better fish coming from the deeper channels and drop-offs. Bream and whiting remain the bread-and-butter species throughout the system, providing consistent fishing for both bait and lure anglers. A few tailor have also been taken by land-based anglers in the Noosaville reaches over the past week. Not a huge amount to report over the last week.  The closer offshore reefs were fishing well, with North Reef producing a reliable mix of snapper and sweetlip while further afield, Sunshine Reef was yielding quality pearl perch, while Double Island Point produced hard-fighting amberjack along with plenty of snapper. Plenty of fish being caught with The Hards, Double Island Point and North Reef all producing quality catches. A wide range of reef species are on the chew, making this one of the most productive times of the year to head offshore. With conditions and water temperatures aligning, both this month and next are shaping up as prime months for reef fishing, with anglers finding quality fish across both the close and wider grounds. The lower estuary continues to produce some quality flathead, while a number of belter bream have also been reported throughout the system. A few smaller mulloway are being caught in the ski run areas, with soft plastic frog-style lures proving effective on the jewies.
reports.credit: Coastwatch (Tin Can Bay section by The Chandlery Bait & Tackle)

reports.text: The new moon is setting up some excellent tides this weekend, and with northerly winds forecast, water temperatures should continue to climb. The big evening high tides will be ideal for chasing quality whiting up on the flats tight against the mangroves. Fresh yabbies remain hard to beat, so it’s worth getting out early to pump a few on the afternoon low. Beach worms are also proving highly effective and continue to account for plenty of fish. The large afternoon low tides will create plenty of opportunities for flathead anglers, with many of the larger drains becoming accessible as water levels drop. There’s also the chance of encountering threadfin salmon and even the odd barramundi in these areas. Mangrove jacks should be firing on the combination of warm water, larger tides and northerly winds. Soft plastics in the 3-5 inch range worked deep into the snags on the back end of the run-out tide are producing fish. Bream and cod are also active around the same structure. Grunter continue to fish well throughout the creek systems. Prawn-style lures and soft vibes are working nicely, while anglers fishing baits are finding success with strips of squid and mullet. Further afield, reports of school and spotted mackerel have come from around Big Mick and Inskip Point. Traditional trolling methods such as planers rigged with small spoons are working, while small hardbodies in the 80-120mm range are also worth a try.
reports.credit: Coastwatch (Tin Can Bay section by The Chandlery Bait & Tackle)

reports.text: Fishing has been fairly consistent through the Noosa River this week, with bream the standout species throughout the Noosaville reaches and up towards the First Lake. A couple of quality flathead have also been reported around Tewantin and Goat Island, while plenty of smaller flathead in the 35-40cm range are being caught between the river mouth and Woods Bay on the drift. For bait anglers, prawns and worms continue to be the most reliable options and are accounting for most of the catches. Full Report pending. North Reef continues to produce quality snapper, pearl perch, kingfish and Moses perch. With plenty of current pushing across the wider grounds, the closer reefs are proving the more fishable option at present and are holding plenty of fish.
